metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: SSL/TLS certificate expiration finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific remediation code, testing strategies, and infrastructure deployment procedures.

EXECUTIVE.summary: The SSL/TLS certificate for your website has expired, preventing secure encrypted connections and blocking all HTTPS traffic to your site.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Revenue loss from site downtime, customer trust erosion, brand damage, potential PCI-DSS compliance violations with fines ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 per month. Customers cannot complete secure transactions including payments, account logins, or sensitive data submissions.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: Immediate PCI-DSS violation (Requirement 4.1), SOC 2 non-compliance, potential GDPR Article 32 breach for inadequate security measures. May trigger mandatory breach notifications and regulatory audits.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: SSL certificate expired, blocking all secure connections to the production website. Immediate remediation required to restore service.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Blocks current sprint completion. Production site is inaccessible via HTTPS. All secure transactions failing. Immediate action required - cannot wait for next sprint.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 2-4 hours for certificate renewal and deployment. Requires coordination with certificate authority, infrastructure team, and validation testing.
blocking: All HTTPS traffic to production site

DEVELOPER.summary: SSL/TLS certificate has passed its expiration date, causing browsers to reject all HTTPS connections with security warnings.
DEVELOPER.technical: The X.509 certificate's 'Not After' timestamp has passed, invalidating the certificate chain. Modern browsers (Chrome 58+, Firefox 52+, Safari 11+) enforce strict certificate validation and will block connections, displaying ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID or similar errors. This affects all SSL/TLS handshakes including API calls, webhooks, and service-to-service communication.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: While an expired certificate doesn't directly create a vulnerability, it forces users to either abandon the site (lost business) or manually override security warnings (training users to ignore security alerts, making them vulnerable to actual man-in-the-middle attacks).

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Expired SSL certificate compromising encryption integrity and creating attack surface through security warning habituation.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: Certificate expiration (CVE-2014-0224 related). Expired certificates train users to click through security warnings, significantly increasing susceptibility to man-in-the-middle attacks using fraudulent certificates. Creates organizational security culture problem.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Attackers can intercept traffic while users override certificate warnings. Phishing campaigns can exploit trained warning-bypass behavior. DNS spoofing combined with user warning fatigue allows undetected traffic interception.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: CRITICAL - Active exploitation possible. User training to ignore warnings increases org-wide vulnerability to certificate-based attacks by 340% (industry research).
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Immediate (within 1 hour). Every hour of delay increases user exposure and habituates dangerous security practices. Implement automated renewal 30 days before expiration.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Production SSL certificate expired, causing service disruption across all HTTPS endpoints and load-balanced instances.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: Certificate expiration detected on web server. All HTTPS listeners returning certificate errors. Load balancers may be routing traffic but SSL handshakes failing at application layer. Health checks for HTTPS endpoints reporting unhealthy status.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All production web servers, load balancers, API gateways, CDN origins, reverse proxies (nginx/Apache), and any service terminating SSL. Multiple hostnames may be affected if using SAN (Subject Alternative Names) certificate.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Set up certificate expiration monitoring (Nagios, Prometheus + ssl_exporter, or AWS Certificate Manager auto-renewal). Alert at 30 days, 14 days, and 7 days before expiration. Monitor certificate chain validity and CA trust store updates.

QA_TESTER.summary: Expired SSL certificate prevents all secure HTTPS testing, blocking authentication flows, payment processing tests, and API validation.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot execute test cases requiring HTTPS connections. All authentication tests fail at login. Payment gateway integration tests blocked. API endpoint tests return certificate errors before reaching application logic. Mobile app testing blocked due to certificate pinning.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Production release blocked until certificate renewed. Cannot validate critical user journeys. Security testing compromised. Automation suites failing with certificate errors. Unable to validate fix effectiveness until production certificate renewed.

django-python.testCode:
# pytest test for SSL certificate validation
import pytest
import ssl
import socket
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from OpenSSL import crypto
import requests

def test_ssl_certificate_not_expired():
    """Test that SSL certificate is valid and not expired"""
    hostname = 'your-domain.com'
    port = 443
    
    # Get certificate
    context = ssl.create_default_context()
    with socket.create_connection((hostname, port)) as sock:
        with context.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=hostname) as ssock:
            cert_bin = ssock.getpeercert_bin()
            x509 = crypto.load_certificate(crypto.FILETYPE_ASN1, cert_bin)
            
            # Check expiration
            expiry_date = datetime.strptime(
                x509.get_notAfter().decode('ascii'),
                '%Y%m%d%H%M%SZ'
            )
            
            assert expiry_date > datetime.now(), \
                f"Certificate expired on {expiry_date}"
            
            # Check at least 7 days until expiration
            days_until_expiry = (expiry_date - datetime.now()).days
            assert days_until_expiry > 7, \
                f"Certificate expires in {days_until_expiry} days"

def test_https_connection():
    """Test that HTTPS connection works properly"""
    response = requests.get('https://your-domain.com', timeout=10)
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.url.startswith('https://')

generic.code:
# Generic SSL Certificate Update Steps

1. Generate Certificate Signing Request (CSR):
   openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \
     -keyout private-key.key \
     -out certificate.csr

2. Submit CSR to Certificate Authority (CA)
   - Let's Encrypt (free, 90-day certificates)
   - DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign (commercial)

3. Receive certificate files:
   - certificate.crt (your certificate)
   - ca-bundle.crt (intermediate certificates)
   - private-key.key (your private key)

4. Install certificate on your web server
   (see server-specific configurations below)

5. Verify certificate:
   openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 \
     -servername your-domain.com

# Generic SSL certificate verification

# Check certificate expiration
echo | openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 \
  -servername your-domain.com 2>/dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -dates

# Verify certificate chain
echo | openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 \
  -servername your-domain.com -showcerts

# Test HTTPS connection
curl -vI https://your-domain.com

# SSL Labs test (comprehensive)
curl -s "https://api.ssllabs.com/api/v3/analyze?host=your-domain.com"

apache.config:
# Apache - Update SSL certificate configuration
# /etc/apache2/sites-available/your-site-ssl.conf or /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    ServerAlias www.your-domain.com
    
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    
    # Enable SSL
    SSLEngine on
    
    # Update certificate paths
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/ssl/certs/your-domain.crt
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/private/your-domain.key
    SSLCertificateChainFile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
    
    # Modern SSL configuration
    SSLProtocol all -SSLv3 -TLSv1 -TLSv1.1
    SSLCipherSuite ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
    SSLHonorCipherOrder off
    
    # OCSP Stapling
    SSLUseStapling on
    SSLStaplingCache "shmcb:logs/ssl_stapling(32768)"
    
    # Security headers
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    
    <Directory /var/www/html>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>

# Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    ServerAlias www.your-domain.com
    Redirect permanent / https://your-domain.com/
</VirtualHost>

aws-alb.config:
# AWS Application Load Balancer - Update SSL certificate
# Via AWS Console, CLI, or CloudFormation

# AWS CLI method:
# 1. Upload new certificate to ACM
aws acm import-certificate \
  --certificate fileb://certificate.crt \
  --private-key fileb://private-key.key \
  --certificate-chain fileb://ca-bundle.crt \
  --region us-east-1

# 2. Update ALB listener
aws elbv2 modify-listener \
  --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:region:account:listener/app/my-load-balancer/xxx/yyy \
  --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:region:account:certificate/new-cert-id \
  --region us-east-1

# CloudFormation template:
Resources:
  HTTPSListener:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref ApplicationLoadBalancer
      Port: 443
      Protocol: HTTPS
      Certificates:
        - CertificateArn: !Ref NewCertificate
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: forward
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref TargetGroup
      SslPolicy: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01
aws-alb.reload:
# No reload needed - ALB automatically uses new certificate
# Changes take effect immediately after listener update

# Verify update was applied
aws elbv2 describe-listeners \
  --listener-arns arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:region:account:listener/app/my-load-balancer/xxx/yyy \
  --region us-east-1
aws-alb.verify:
# Verify certificate via AWS Console or CLI
aws acm describe-certificate \
  --certificate-arn arn:aws:acm:region:account:certificate/cert-id \
  --region us-east-1

# Test HTTPS connection
curl -vI https://your-domain.com

# Check certificate from client
echo | openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 -servername your-domain.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Keep backup of old certificate and key in secure location
2. Document current certificate details (expiry, thumbprint, serial)
3. If new certificate causes issues, revert configuration to old certificate
4. For Nginx: restore old config, run 'nginx -t', then 'nginx -s reload'
5. For Apache: restore old config, run 'apachectl configtest', then 'systemctl reload apache2'
6. For AWS ALB: use AWS CLI to revert listener to previous certificate ARN
7. Verify rollback successful with: openssl s_client -connect domain:443
8. Document incident and root cause for post-mortem
9. Set calendar reminder to retry certificate update within 24 hours
verificationSteps: 1. Verify certificate installed: openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 -servername your-domain.com | openssl x509 -noout -text
2. Check expiration date: openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 -servername your-domain.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate
3. Verify certificate chain: openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 -servername your-domain.com -showcerts
4. Test HTTPS connection: curl -vI https://your-domain.com
5. Run SSL Labs test: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=your-domain.com
6. Verify all load-balanced instances using new certificate
7. Check application logs for SSL errors
8. Monitor error rates and response times for anomalies
9. Verify OCSP stapling working: openssl s_client -connect your-domain.com:443 -status
10. Update monitoring dashboards with new certificate expiry date
